settings.heading: Which cufflink fitting suits the wearer?
settings.body:
The fitting is the part most people never think about and the part they use every day. Bullet backs, a bar that swivels through the cuff, are the quickest to put on and the most common. Whale backs work the same way with a flat bar and hold heavier fronts better. Chain links, a front and back joined by a short chain, are slower to fasten and the most comfortable once on.

  • Cufflinks need a double (French) cuff, or a convertible cuff with two buttonholes.
  • Engraving adds initials, a date, coordinates or a crest; we proof it before it is cut.
  • Hallmarked: 9ct gold 375, 18ct 750, platinum 950.

settings.title: Do cufflinks need a special shirt?
settings.content: Yes. Cufflinks fasten a double cuff, also called a French cuff, which folds back on itself and has buttonholes on both sides and no buttons. A convertible cuff, with a button and a second buttonhole, also takes them. A standard button cuff will not.

settings.title: Which cufflink fitting is easiest to use?
settings.content: Bullet backs: the bar swivels in line with the post, slides through both buttonholes, then turns across to lock. Whale backs work the same way with a flat tail. Chain links take longer to fasten but have no moving parts to wear out. For a gift, a bullet back is the safe choice.

settings.title: Gold or platinum?
settings.content: 9ct gold, hallmarked 375, is harder-wearing and paler. 18ct, hallmarked 750, has a deeper colour and is the usual choice for an heirloom pair. Platinum, hallmarked 950, is the heaviest and stays white without plating. All three are solid precious metal, never plated, so engraving cannot wear through to another metal.

settings.title: Can you engrave cufflinks?
settings.content: Yes: initials, a monogram, a date, coordinates, a short phrase, a signature taken from a photograph, or a family crest. Flat oval, round or rectangular fronts take engraving best. We send you a proof before anything is cut, and hand engraving adds about a week to the making time.

settings.title: How far ahead should I order cufflinks for a wedding?
settings.content: We confirm the making and engraving time when you order, so order as early as you can, especially for a groomsmen set with different initials. Tell us the date and we will say honestly whether we can make it.

settings.title: Can you make cufflinks from a family piece or with my own stones?
settings.content: Yes. We can set an inherited stone or engrave a crest or signature. We design in CAD and show you the render before making anything, so you see exactly what you will receive.

settings.title: Can I return cufflinks?
settings.content: Cufflinks are made or engraved to order for you, so we do not offer change-of-mind returns, which is why we send a proof first. If a pair arrives faulty or not as ordered, you can reject it for a full refund within 30 days; after that we repair or replace it.

settings.heading: Our commitment to you
settings.body:
• Every centre and loose diamond comes with a GIA or IGI certificate. Stones in multi-stone pieces are not individually certified; the listing states their grade.
  • Lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects.
  • Free inspection and cleaning for life.
  • Every engraving proofed before it is cut.
  • If a piece arrives faulty or not as ordered, you can reject it for a full refund within 30 days; after that we repair or replace it.
  • Made-to-order and bespoke pieces are made for you, so we talk each order through before we start. Ready-made pieces can be returned within 14 days of delivery, unworn and in their original packaging.
